title: Continuous reduction near a fixed diagonal rank locus
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and A its coefficient-extension integer ring [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], with the maximal-ideal-adic topology. Let pi generate its maximal ideal. Let T be any topological space, m,n,r natural numbers with r <= min(m,n), and e : Fin r -> Nat monotone. Let D be the n by m matrix whose (i,j) entry is pi^(e i) when i=j and i<r and is zero otherwise. If F : T -> Mat(n,m,A) has continuous entries, t0 : T satisfies F(t0)=D, and rank(F(t)) <= r for every t, then there is an open neighbourhood U of t0 and maps L : U -> GL(n,A), R : U -> GL(m,A), with all entries of L, R and their inverses continuous, such that L(t) F(t) R(t)=D for every t in U. Empty dimensions and r=0 are allowed.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.12(2), finite extension case; auxiliary fixed-diagonal induction.

proof.text: Let N be the maximum of the finitely many exponents, or zero when r=0. Continuity gives an open neighbourhood V on which all entries of F-D lie in (pi)^N. For each pivot column k<r, divide its error by pi^(e k), filling the other columns with zero, to form a square n by n matrix B. These quotients are uniquely determined since pi is nonzero. Cancellation in the principal-ideal neighbourhood bases proves their continuity: to control the quotient modulo pi^a, control its multiple modulo pi^(a+e k). At the centre B=0.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.12(2), finite extension case; auxiliary fixed-diagonal induction.

proof.text: Set M=1+B. Its determinant is one at the centre. Units form an open set in the maximal-ideal-adic topology of the local ring, so restrict to the open unit-determinant locus U0. M is invertible there, and its inverse is continuous by the adjugate formula and continuity of inversion on units. The first r columns of M D equal those of F by the definition of B. Thus G=M^(-1) F has its first r columns equal to D.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.12(2), finite extension case; auxiliary fixed-diagonal induction.

proof.text: Every entry in an extra column of F is divisible by each pivot pi^(e k), since D vanishes in those columns and F-D is divisible by pi^N. Multiplication by M^(-1) preserves this divisibility. Divide the first r rows of the extra columns of G by their corresponding pivots to get q, supported only at row indices <r and column indices >=r. These quotients are again unique and continuous. Consequently q squared is zero, R=1-q has inverse 1+q, and G R agrees with D whenever the row or the column index is <r.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.12(2), finite extension case; auxiliary fixed-diagonal induction.

proof.text: Any nonzero entry of the remaining bottom-right block would give an (r+1) by (r+1) diagonal minor with nonzero determinant, using the first r rows and columns and that entry. Over the domain its rank would be r+1, contradicting rank(G R)<=rank(F)<=r. Therefore G R=D. Transport U0 through the open subtype inclusion into T and use L=M^(-1). The same formulas handle r=0, empty dimensions and exponent-zero pivots.
